stem: What type of visual field defect are you likely to see in a lesion of the visual cortex:
options: Contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing
fact: A lesion of the visual cortex results in a contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing.
mnemonic: Visual cortex keeps the macula: homonymous loss with macular sparing.
finding: Source page displays contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing as correct.

stem: A patient complains of diplopia on reading or walking downstairs, which of the following cranial nerves is most likely to be affected:
options: Ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve
fact: Trochlear nerve palsy causes weakness of downward gaze, vertical diplopia, and difficulty reading or walking downstairs.
mnemonic: SO4: superior oblique is supplied by CN IV.
finding: Source page displays trochlear nerve as correct.

stem: A 64 year old lady complains of a sore right eye. On examination, you note a normal corneal blink reflex on her left side but no consensual blink reflex on her right side. A lesion in which of the following structures is most likely to cause this clinical picture:
fact: The ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve is the afferent limb of the corneal reflex, and the facial nerve is the efferent limb. Loss of the right consensual response indicates a right facial efferent lesion.
mnemonic: V1 senses, VII closes the eye.
finding: Source page displays facial nerve as correct.

stem: Oculomotor (CN III) palsy with sparing of the pupillary reflex is most likely caused by which of the following:
options: Aneurysm of the posterior communicating artery
fact: Diabetic ischaemic oculomotor palsy usually spares the pupil, whereas compressive aneurysmal palsy commonly involves the pupil.
mnemonic: Diabetes spares the pupil; compression involves it.
finding: Source page displays diabetes mellitus as correct.

stem: Which of the following clinical features would you most expect to see in a glossopharyngeal nerve palsy:
fact: Glossopharyngeal nerve palsy can cause loss of the afferent limb of the gag reflex. Hoarseness and uvular deviation are more typical of vagal dysfunction.
mnemonic: IX initiates the gag; X executes it.
finding: Source page displays loss of gag reflex as correct.

stem: Which of the following nerves is the afferent pathway of the gag reflex:
fact: The glossopharyngeal nerve is the afferent limb of the gag reflex; the vagus nerve is the efferent limb.
finding: Source page displays glossopharyngeal nerve as correct.

stem: A patient complains of headaches and dizziness. Imaging reveals a tumour at the cerebellopontine angle. Which of the following nerves will most likely be affected by this tumour:
fact: The vestibulocochlear nerve is closely associated with the cerebellopontine angle and commonly affected by lesions there; the facial nerve also travels with it.
mnemonic: CPA: VIII is the classic nerve at the cerebellopontine angle.
finding: Source page displays vestibulocochlear nerve as correct.

stem: Regarding the abducens nerve, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: The abducens nerve innervates the inferior oblique muscle.
Abducens nerve palsy results in a vertical diplopia.
The abducens nerve originates in the medulla.
The abducens nerve enters the orbit through the inferior orbital fissure.
Abducens nerve palsy results in a convergent squint.
fact: The abducens nerve arises from the pons, enters the orbit through the superior orbital fissure, and innervates the lateral rectus. Palsy causes horizontal diplopia and a convergent squint.
mnemonic: LR6: lateral rectus is supplied by CN VI.
finding: Source page displays convergent squint as correct.

stem: A 64 year old lady presents to ED with headaches. Imaging show a tumour compressing the structures in the internal auditory meatus. Which of the following structures are most likely affected:
options: Internal jugular vein and trigeminal nerve
fact: The internal auditory meatus transmits the facial and vestibulocochlear nerves.
mnemonic: Internal auditory meatus: VII and VIII travel together.
finding: Source page displays facial and vestibulocochlear nerve as correct.

stem: A patient complains of diplopia and on examination is found to have a depressed and abducted eye with ptosis. Which of the following nerves is most likely to be affected:
options: Ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve
fact: Oculomotor nerve palsy produces a down-and-out eye with ptosis and diplopia because most extraocular muscles and levator palpebrae are affected.
mnemonic: CN III: down and out with ptosis.
finding: Source page displays oculomotor nerve as correct.
